Descriptive statistics of a Delphi study

Source: R/describe.R
delphi_describe.Rd

Computes, for every item, round and indicator, the number of ratings and the usual Delphi summaries: mean, standard deviation, median, quartiles, interquartile range (IQR), range and coefficient of variation.

Usage

delphi_describe(
  x,
  round = NULL,
  indicator = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  type = 7,
  relative_to = c("points", "range")
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

round, indicator, items

Optional subsets: round numbers, indicator labels and item names to keep. NULL keeps all.

type

Quantile algorithm passed to stats::quantile(). The default 7 is R's default; use 6 to match SPSS and Minitab, which many Delphi studies report.

relative_to

How the relative IQR (iqr_rel) is computed: "points" (default) divides the IQR by the number of points of the scale, max - min + 1; "range" divides it by max - min. See delphi_consensus().

Value

A data frame of class delphi_describe with one row per indicator, round and item and columns indicator, round, item, n, missing, mean, sd, median, q1, q3, iqr, iqr_rel, min, max and cv.

Details

iqr_rel is the IQR as a share of the rating scale, so that dispersion can be compared between indicators rated on different scales (for example from 1 to 10 and from 1 to 100). cv is the standard deviation divided by the mean.

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
d <- delphi_describe(x)
head(d)
#>  indicator round item  n missing mean   sd median   q1  q3  iqr iqr_rel min max
#>     impact     1   E1 15       0 6.93 1.44      7 6.50 8.0 1.50    0.15   4   9
#>     impact     1   E2 15       0 5.13 1.73      5 4.00 7.0 3.00    0.30   2   8
#>     impact     1   E3 15       0 6.13 1.36      7 5.00 7.0 2.00    0.20   4   8
#>     impact     1   E4 15       0 7.13 1.51      7 6.00 8.0 2.00    0.20   5  10
#>     impact     1   E5 15       0 5.47 3.07      4 3.00 8.5 5.50    0.55   2   9
#>     impact     1   E6 14       1 3.64 2.37      3 1.25 5.0 3.75    0.38   1   8
#>    cv
#>  0.21
#>  0.34
#>  0.22
#>  0.21
#>  0.56
#>  0.65

# Only the impact ratings of round 2, with SPSS-style quartiles
delphi_describe(x, round = 2, indicator = "impact", type = 6)
